summary: Full published-paper extraction, including Granville's §12 addendum: 151 items (9 pinned-library, 12 already planned, 130 missing), with every missing item routed once across five source routes, three Part II continuations and one new progression-specific modular-method roadmap. The main theorem is an effective prime-exponent bound and fixed-length finiteness, not Erdős nonexistence. Printed errors and proof gaps are retained visibly, including a corrected Frey discriminant and order-four point, conductor bookkeeping, and the insufficient Roth threshold; the executable original-proof endgame uses exp(exp(10^7)). Complete means extraction/routing complete, not a closed blueprint, verified original-source proof for every prerequisite, or formalization. Independent review (REV-PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20) corrected the file in place: 152 items (11 library, 12 planned, 129 missing), nine source routes, two Part II continuations and one new roadmap; every change is listed in research/blueprint/reviews/REV-PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20.md.

items.name: Primitive nontrivial progression solution
items.statement: S(n,d,k,y,ell) means n,d,y are integers, k is a positive integer, ell is prime, gcd(n,d)=1, product_{0<=i<k}(n+i*d)=y^ell, and y*d!=0. Thus every progression term is nonzero. H means S together with k>=10^8 and ell>exp(10^k); Hplus means H and k>=2*10^10.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Effective bound for the prime exponent
items.statement: There exists an effectively computable absolute positive constant k0 such that, for every positive integer k>=k0, integers n,d,y with gcd(n,d)=1, and prime ell satisfying product_{0<=i<k}(n+i*d)=y^ell, either y=0, d=0, or ell<=exp(10^k).
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Weierstrass coefficients and invariant convention
items.statement: Over a commutative ring R a WeierstrassCurve has coefficients a1,a2,a3,a4,a6 and equation Y^2+a1*X*Y+a3*Y=X^3+a2*X^2+a4*X+a6. Its b2=a1^2+4*a2, b4=2*a4+a1*a3, b6=a3^2+4*a6, b8=a1^2*a6+4*a2*a6-a1*a3*a4+a2*a3^2-a4^2, and Delta=-b2^2*b8-8*b4^3-27*b6^2+9*b2*b4*b6.
items.locator: Underlying construction used in Sections 2, 3 and 6; especially Lemma 3.2, p. 361
items.note: Pinned Mathlib Weierstrass.lean definitions reread. Infrastructure only: the two specialized Frey discriminant identities are separately extracted. Reviewer: the curve equation itself is mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Equation (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Affine/Basic.lean:149, with equation_iff).

items.name: Reduced level of an elliptic residual representation
items.statement: For an elliptic curve E/Q of conductor M and nonzero minimal discriminant Delta, and prime ell>=3, rho_{E,ell} is the G_Q-action on E[ell]. Set M0=M/product{q prime: ord_q(M)=1 and ell divides ord_q(Delta)}. The notation ord_q is the integer valuation, not q raised to that valuation.
items.note: The residual carrier is imported separately in item 130. M0 is the paper's explicit level quotient, not automatically the prime-to-ell Artin conductor when ell divides the elliptic conductor.

items.name: Weight-two newform at the reduced level
items.statement: For E,ell,M0 as in item 04, if E[ell] is irreducible, there is a normalized cuspidal newform f=sum c_n*q^n of weight 2, level M0 and trivial nebentypus, with totally real coefficient field K=Q(c_n:n>=1) and a prime lambda of K above ell, such that rho_{E,ell} and the residual representation of f at lambda become isomorphic after extending both coefficient fields to an algebraic closure of F_ell.
items.note: Source theorem quoted in full. Route to the existing optimizer; certify the local/coefficient-prime cases, using elliptic modularity and R19 rather than an assumed modularity predicate.

items.name: Good-prime trace congruence
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 3, for a rational prime p not dividing ell*M*M0, a_p(E) is congruent to c_p modulo lambda.
items.note: These stages explicitly compare good-prime Frobenius polynomials on the actual elliptic and modular realizations. Reduction at lambda gives this congruence; no implemented comparison is claimed. Reviewer: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.2 (cohomological Hilbert forms) replaced by R19.1, which plans the weight-two representation from Jacobian cohomology with "the unramified characteristic polynomial by the geometric Eichler–Shimura relation".

items.name: Removed multiplicative-prime trace congruence
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 3, if p is prime, p does not divide ell*M0, and ord_p(M)=1, then p+1 is congruent to either c_p or -c_p modulo lambda.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Exponent bound from a removed prime
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 3, if p!=ell is prime, ord_p(M)=1 and ell divides ord_p(Delta), then ell<=(sqrt(p)+1)^((M0+1)/6).
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Kraus comparison threshold
items.statement: For a positive integer N put mu(N)=N*product_{q prime,q|N}(1+1/q), gplus(N)=dim S_2^new(N), F(N)=(sqrt(mu(N)/6)+1)^(2*gplus(N)), G(N)=(sqrt(mu(lcm(N,4))/6)+1)^2, and H_Kraus(N)=max(F(N),G(N)).
items.locator: Section 2, equation (5) and following display, p. 360
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Kraus full-two-torsion realization
items.statement: For an elliptic curve E/Q with full rational 2-torsion, prime ell>=5, irreducible residual representation of Serre weight 2, and prime-to-ell residual conductor N, if ell>H_Kraus(N), there is an elliptic curve F/Q of conductor N with full rational 2-torsion and rho(F,ell) isomorphic to rho(E,ell). In the progression application the optimizer must prove N=M0 before invoking this statement.
items.note: Kraus 1997 Theorem 4 is the authoritative hypothesis-complete version. Elliptic modularity supplies his modularity hypothesis. Bennett–Siksek Theorem 4 suppresses the weight/coefficient-prime comparison; this is an explicit adapter in the design, not an automatic identification of N with the level quotient M0.

items.name: Gcd of two progression terms
items.statement: Assume S. For 0<=i<j<k, the positive gcd of n+i*d and n+j*d divides j-i.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Large-prime valuations are divisible by ell
items.statement: Assume S. If 0<=i<k and q>=k is prime, then ell divides ord_q(n+i*d), with valuation taken on the absolute value of the nonzero integer.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Small-prime factors with an explicit sign convention
items.statement: Assume S and ell odd. Each term has a unique factorization n+i*d=A_i*y_i^ell where A_i is a positive integer all of whose prime factors are <k and y_i is a nonzero integer all of whose prime factors in |y_i| are >=k. All powers of primes <k belong to A_i.
items.note: Odd ell is essential for negative progression terms. Ai contains every small-prime power; it is not the ell-power-free part.

items.name: Three-term progression and its Frey curve
items.statement: Assume S with ell odd. Let A be the triples (i,j,2*j-i) with 0<=i<j and 2*j-i<k. For a=(i,j,h) in A put g=gcd(n+i*d,2*(n+j*d),n+h*d)>0, a_a=(n+i*d)/g, b_a=-2*(n+j*d)/g, c_a=(n+h*d)/g. These are nonzero coprime integers with a_a+b_a+c_a=0. The Frey curve is E_a: Y^2=X*(X-a_a)*(X+c_a).
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: The first generalized Fermat identity
items.statement: With the factorization and triple of items 13-14, A_i*y_i^ell-2*A_j*y_j^ell+A_{2*j-i}*y_{2*j-i}^ell=0.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: First Frey discriminant in the pinned convention
items.statement: For the Weierstrass model in item 14, Delta(E_a)=16*(a_a*b_a*c_a)^2=2^6*g^(-6)*(n+i*d)^2*(n+j*d)^2*(n+(2*j-i)*d)^2.
items.locator: Lemma 3.2 discriminant display, p. 361; corrected normalization
items.note: Corrected polynomial identity: printed 64(abc)^2 is false for the displayed Weierstrass model; pinned Delta yields 16(abc)^2. Odd-prime valuations unchanged; no 2-adic minimal-discriminant identity is inferred.

items.name: First Frey model at odd primes
items.statement: Assume S, ell odd, and a in A. The model E_a is minimal and semistable at every odd prime.
items.note: Large-prime valuation conclusion split into item 132. General minimal-model carriers and reduction tests are imported, not duplicated.

items.name: First Frey reduced level divides its small coefficients
items.statement: Assume S with ell>=7 and a=(i,j,h) in A. A weight-two newform realizes rho(E_a,ell) at the reduced level M_a; M_a divides 2^8*A_i*A_j*A_h.
items.note: Irreducibility is item 59; squarefreeness of the odd part is item 133. This is the progression specialization, not a second level-lowering theorem.

items.name: First Frey exponential level bound
items.statement: Under item 18, M_a <= 2^7*exp(1.000081*k).
items.note: Prime-product divisibility split into item 134; analytic input 65. The factor 2^8 bound is a general conductor bound, not the erroneous discriminant normalization.

items.name: Equal-sum quadruples and the second Frey curve
items.statement: Assume S with ell odd. For 0<=j1<i1<=i2<j2<k and i1+i2=j1+j2 define A=(n+j1*d)*(n+j2*d), B=(n+i1*d)*(n+i2*d), kappa=j1*j2-i1*i2. Then A-B=kappa*d^2, kappa!=0 and |kappa|<k^2. Define E_i: Y^2=X*(X^2+2*kappa*d*X+kappa*A).
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Second Frey discriminant
items.statement: For the model of item 20, Delta(E_i)=-64*kappa^3*A^2*B.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Second Frey local properties
items.statement: Under item 20, if p>=k is prime and p does not divide kappa, the displayed model is minimal and semistable at p.
items.note: Valuation divisibility is item 135. In §4 use the separately verified local c4/Delta test in item 136, since p there need not be >=k.

items.name: Second Frey reduced level bound
items.statement: Assume S with ell>=11 and a quadruple as in item 20. A weight-two newform realizes rho(E_i,ell) at its reduced level M_i, and M_i<=2^7*3^5*k^4*exp(2.000162*k).
items.note: Irreducibility imported from item 60; finer divisibility is item 137. The bound concerns the reduced level, not necessarily the conductor of E_i itself.

items.name: Primes in the top half of the interval divide d
items.statement: Assume H. For every prime p with k/2<p<=k, p divides d.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Actual elliptic curves at the reduced levels
items.statement: Assume H. For every a in A there exists an elliptic curve F_a/Q with full rational 2-torsion, conductor M_a, and rho_{F_a,ell} isomorphic to rho_{E_a,ell}.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Good reduction and equality of integer traces
items.statement: Assume H, a in A, and p prime with k/2<p<=k. Both E_a and F_a have good reduction at p, and their integer traces a_p are equal.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Forced supersingular primes
items.statement: Under item 26, if p is 3 modulo 4 then a_p(F_a)=0, and F_a has supersingular reduction at p.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Legendre parameters and their six transforms
items.statement: For lambda in Q minus {0,1}, let F_lambda: Y^2=X*(X-1)*(X-lambda). A rational elliptic curve with full rational 2-torsion is a quadratic twist of a Legendre model; its parameters are lambda, 1/lambda, 1-lambda, 1/(1-lambda), (lambda-1)/lambda, lambda/(lambda-1), allowing coincidences.
items.locator: Section 6, equation (17) and adjacent discussion, pp. 366-367
items.note: Six entries need not be distinct (e.g. lambda=-1). Existing quadraticTwistOf is a supplier, not a theorem constructing the Legendre normalization from full rational 2-torsion.

items.name: Good odd primes are units for both Legendre factors
items.statement: Let F/Q have full rational 2-torsion, be semistable at odd primes, have conductor M, and let lambda be any associated Legendre parameter. At every odd prime p of good reduction for F, ord_p(lambda)=ord_p(1-lambda)=0.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Quadratic-character odd conductor is supported on the curve conductor
items.statement: Under item 29, let omega be 1,-1,2 or -2. The primitive quadratic character associated to the rational squareclass omega*lambda, characterized away from 2 and the support of lambda by chi(p)=(omega*lambda/p), has odd conductor dividing M.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Finite-field two-by-four torsion
items.statement: For a prime p congruent to 3 modulo 4 and eta in F_p minus {0,1,-1}, the elliptic curve Y^2=X*(X-1)*(X-eta^2) has a subgroup of F_p-points isomorphic to Z/2Z times Z/4Z.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Legendre nonsquare condition in the residue class 3 modulo 8
items.statement: Assume H and a in A. For any associated Legendre parameter lambda of F_a and prime p with k/2<p<=k and p=3 modulo 8, the Legendre symbol (lambda/p) is -1.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Finite-field two-descent homomorphism
items.statement: For p odd and lambda in Q minus {0,1} with ord_p(lambda)=ord_p(1-lambda)=0, the descent homomorphism from F_lambda(F_p) to (F_p^*/F_p^{*2})^3 has coordinates given on affine non-2-torsion points by x, x-1, x-lambda modulo squares, takes the identity to (1,1,1), and has kernel 2*F_lambda(F_p). At a 2-torsion point its two nonzero coordinates determine the third by the product-one condition.
items.locator: Section 6, Legendre elliptic curves revisited, p. 370
items.note: Reviewer correction: pinned Tau Ceti has the x−θ descent homomorphism μ : Multiplicative W.Point →* W.M into the square classes of the étale algebra K[X]/(f) (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/MordellWeil/XSubT.lean:817) and ker_μ_eq (line 991): its kernel is exactly 2·W(K), over any field of characteristic ≠ 2 (planned by Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 6, "the x − θ map into the étale algebra A = K[X]/(f)"). The item is the case f = X(X−1)(X−λ) over F_p, read through the CRT identification F_p[X]/(f) ≅ F_p^3; that identification is a routine adapter, stated as one lemma in the design, not new mathematics.

items.name: Exact two-adic order for the j=1728 model
items.statement: For p prime congruent to 5 modulo 8, the cardinality of F_{-1}(F_p), where F_{-1}:Y^2=X*(X-1)*(X+1), has 2-adic valuation exactly 3.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: The second Legendre squareclass case
items.statement: Assume H. If an associated parameter lambda of F_a has lambda=2*t^2 and 1-lambda=2*v^2 with positive rational t,v, then for every prime p=5 modulo 8 with k/2<p<=k, ord_p(t)=ord_p(v)=0 and (t*v/p)=1.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Characters forced by the Frey families
items.statement: Assume Hplus. For each a in A one can choose a primitive quadratic character chi_a of conductor N_a such that simultaneously the conclusions in items 37-39 hold.
items.locator: Proposition 6.1 and its two-case construction, pp. 366-373
items.note: One choice simultaneously satisfies 37–39; all later subsets use this fixed family. Case I and Case II are separately inventoried.

items.name: Large prime-weighted character sum
items.statement: For the characters chosen simultaneously in item 36, |sum_{k/2<m<=k}chi_a(m)*Lambda(m)|>0.1239*k for every a in A. Lambda is the von Mangoldt function and m ranges over integers, including prime powers.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Odd conductor divisibility
items.statement: For the characters chosen in item 36, N_a^odd divides M_a, where N_a^odd=N_a/2^ord_2(N_a).
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Nontrivial odd conductor
items.statement: For the characters chosen in item 36, N_a^odd!=1. In particular chi_a is nonprincipal.
items.locator: Proposition 6.1, p. 367; Case II exclusion, pp. 372–373
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Exceptional real zero
items.statement: Fix the effective absolute c_star>0 furnished by Proposition 7.1. For a nontrivial primitive quadratic character chi of conductor N, an exceptional zero is a real zero beta of L(s,chi) with 1-c_star/log(N)<beta<1. Its conductor is called exceptional.
items.locator: Section 7, Proposition 7.1 and following paragraph, pp. 373-374
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Repulsion of exceptional conductors
items.statement: With c_star from Proposition 7.1, two distinct exceptional quadratic conductors N1<N2 satisfy N2>N1^2.
items.note: Existence/uniqueness/simplicity and the two-zero inequality are split into items 87–88.

items.name: Contradiction from a harmonic family of very smooth conductors
items.statement: Assume Hplus and fix 0<c1<1. If D is a subset of A with pairwise distinct largest prime factors P(N_a), all P(N_a)<(log(k))^(1-c1), and sum_{a in D}1/P(N_a)>=0.166, then k<=k1(c1) for an effectively computable constant depending only on c1.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Largest prime factor of a quadratic conductor
items.statement: If N>1 is the conductor of a primitive quadratic character, then P(N)>0.94*log(N).
items.note: N>1 excludes the conductor-one principal character. The finite prime-product check at small N is essential; minimum P(N)/log N occurs at N=24. Broad AN.5 scope is not a pre-existing numerical theorem.

items.name: Cancellation between two distinct smooth characters
items.statement: For every c2>0 there are effective k3(c2)>0 and c3(c2)>0 such that if k>=k3(c2), and chi1,chi2 are distinct primitive quadratic characters of conductors N1,N2 with P(N_i)<=k^(7/16) and N_i<=k^c2, then |sum_{k/2<m<=k}chi1(m)*chi2(m)|<=k^(1-c3).
items.note: Generic analytic result, independent of progression solutions. Repair ambient modulus versus primitive conductor and use eventual divisor subpower bounds; report D2–D3.

items.name: Bombieri-Selberg inner-product inequality
items.statement: If m>=1 and x,y1,...,ym lie in a real or complex inner product space, then sum_i |<x,yi>|^2 <= ||x||^2 * max_i sum_j |<yi,yj>|.
items.note: Pinned-library and atlas comparison: see report audit groups and the unique route. No declaration proving this source-specific statement was found.

items.name: Three-term progression existence at positive density
items.statement: For every real 0<delta<1 there is a positive K0(delta) such that for every integer k>=K0(delta), any J subset {0,...,k-1} with |J|>=delta*k contains i<j with i,j,2*j-i in J.
items.note: Full pinned Mathlib Combinatorics/Additive/Corner/Roth.lean read. Its explicit tower-type threshold supplies this qualitative existential result, not Rahman's much smaller double-exponential formula (item 101). Unpack ThreeAPFree and order the three distinct natural numbers.

items.name: Simultaneous thin-prime avoidance and polynomial conductor
items.statement: Assume Hplus and k>=exp(exp(10^6)). For any set S of primes <=k with sum_{p in S}1/p<0.17, there exists one a in A such that simultaneously: no p in S divides N_a; P(N_a)<=k^(7/16); no prime in ((log(k))^(1-10^(-4)),10^4*log(k)] divides N_a; and N_a<k^418.
items.note: Literal Proposition 9.1 target, including the printed threshold. Its claimed Roth comparison is numerically false: 132*log(2)/10^(-5)>10^6. Do not treat the printed proof as certifying this threshold. Item 149 supplies a proved-safe weakened threshold exp(exp(10^7)); all simultaneous conclusions and exponent 418 are unchanged. A design claiming the sharper threshold must acquire an additional quantitative argument.

items.name: Erdos maximal-valuation deletion
items.statement: Under the small-prime factorization of item 13, let J be any subset of {0,...,k-1}. For each prime p<k occurring in the A_i for i in J, remove an index with maximal ord_p(A_i). The remaining set J1 loses at most pi(k) indices and product_{i in J1}A_i divides (k-1)!.
items.note: Full elementary valuation proof in report: for surviving i, vp(Ai)<=vp(i-ip); multiply over distances to ip. No positivity of the progression terms is required.

items.name: Exceptional moduli for the addendum
items.statement: For sufficiently large integer k, fix the constant c from the applicable bounded-height Landau-Page zero-free statement and put T=exp(c*log(k)/(3*log(log(k)))). Let Q(k) be the integers 1<=q<=k^4 for which some primitive character modulo q has a zero beta+i*t with |t|<=T and beta>1-3*log(log(k))/log(k).
items.note: Bounded zero height is explicit. Q(k) is a set of moduli admitting at least one bad primitive character, not a multiset of zeros or of characters.

items.name: Finiteness for each fixed sufficiently large progression length
items.statement: For each fixed integer k>=k0, there are finitely many positive integer tuples (n,d,y,ell), ell>=2, gcd(n,d)=1, with product_{i=0}^{k-1}(n+i*d)=y^ell. The signed version is for fixed k and yd!=0, not one finite set as k varies.
items.note: Deduce from the exponent bound and fixed-exponent finiteness, reducing composite exponents to prime factors and separately ruling out y=±1 for large k. This is ineffective finiteness of points, not a certified enumeration algorithm.

items.name: Erdős–Selfridge theorem (background endpoint)
items.statement: There are no positive integers n,k,y,ell with k>=2, ell>=2 and n(n+1)...(n+k-1)=y^ell.
items.note: Historical theorem, not used as an assumption of the proof of Theorem 2. Retained as a background statement-register entry; the new roadmap must not silently make its separately sourced proof a prerequisite of Theorem 2.

items.name: Erdős nonexistence conjecture
items.statement: Define the conjectural assertion: an absolute k0 exists such that for k>=k0 the primitive progression product has no positive integer solution with ell>=2. This is stronger than fixed-k finiteness and is not proved in this paper.
items.note: Statement register only; no theorem consumer may assume this conjecture.

items.name: Faltings rational-point finiteness input
items.statement: A smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least 2 over a number field has finitely many rational points.
items.note: RP.4 explicitly owns the Parshin/Shafarevich proof route. Fixed-exponent covering and genus verification remain the application adapter, item 129.

items.name: Normalized cuspidal newform carrier
items.statement: At nonzero level N and weight 2 use the normalized cusp form in the new subspace with Hecke eigenconditions away from N and fixed nebentypus. The first q-coefficient is 1; the full eigencondition at bad indices is a theorem, not a new field in the carrier.
items.note: Pinned Newforms/Newform.lean definitions read. Trivial nebentypus is an explicit restriction in this paper.

items.name: Algebraicity and integrality of newform coefficients
items.statement: For a normalized newform of weight at least 2 the field Q(c_n:n>=1) is a number field and each c_n is an algebraic integer.
items.note: Reviewed ModularForms Layer 8 audit reports this absent at the pin; its README explicitly plans it. AINTLIB provenance is not pinned Tau Ceti availability.

items.name: Coefficient-field conjugates and dimension
items.statement: For a weight-two normalized newform of trivial nebentypus and level N, its coefficient field is totally real and [K:Q]<=dim_C S_2^new(Gamma0(N)); all embeddings yield conjugate normalized newforms of the same level.
items.note: Galois-stability/orbit-degree and real good Hecke spectrum give the comparison; not arbitrary coefficientwise conjugation of analytic limits.

items.name: Martin weight-two newspace dimension bound
items.statement: For every positive integer N, dim_C S_2^new(Gamma0(N)) <= (N+1)/12.
items.note: Original published statement inspected. General dimension formulas and old/new decomposition are suppliers, but this sharp uniform numerical inequality is not a named existing atlas target.

items.name: All-conjugates weight-two coefficient bound
items.statement: For a normalized weight-two newform of level N and trivial nebentypus, at a prime p not dividing N and for every embedding sigma of its coefficient field into C, |sigma(c_p)|<=2*sqrt(p).
items.note: Weight-two abelian quotient/Tate realization plus all-embeddings Weil bound; no assertion that analytic ModularForms proves general Ramanujan–Deligne.

items.name: Irreducibility with full rational two-torsion
items.statement: If E/Q has full rational 2-torsion and ell>=7 is prime, E[ell] is irreducible as a G_Q-module.
items.note: Requires exact rational-isogeny classification consequences, not just finiteness of exceptional primes for a fixed E.

items.name: Irreducibility with a rational point of order two
items.statement: If E/Q has a rational point of order 2 and ell>=11 is prime, E[ell] is irreducible.
items.note: Keep this distinct from the full-two-torsion ell>=7 statement and from torsion-point classification alone.

items.name: Local conductor-exponent bounds
items.statement: For E/Q, its elliptic/Artin conductor exponent at 2 is at most 8, at 3 at most 5, and at primes p>=5 at most 2; good reduction gives exponent 0 and multiplicative reduction exponent 1.
items.note: Reviewer correction: neither cited layer states these bounds. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 4 plans only the algorithmic (Ogg) exponent and names the comparison with the Artin exponent as a separate project; ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.3 defines conductors and promises "the precise comparison with the conductor of an elliptic curve", with wild contributions at 2 and 3, but does not state f_2<=8, f_3<=5, f_p<=2. Neither pinned library has conductor exponents of elliptic curves over Q. Routed as a source of R01.3 (route 12).

items.name: Second generalized Fermat identity
items.statement: For the quadruple of item 20, A_j1*A_j2*(y_j1*y_j2)^ell - A_i1*A_i2*(y_i1*y_i2)^ell = kappa*d^2.
items.note: Source-specific statement audited against the pinned libraries and existing stage contracts; see the report and its assigned route.

items.name: General three-index linear identity
items.statement: For integers i1<i2<i3, (i3-i2)(n+i1*d)+(i1-i3)(n+i2*d)+(i2-i1)(n+i3*d)=0. Applying the small/large-prime factorization gives a generalized Fermat equation of signature (ell,ell,ell).
items.note: Source-specific statement audited against the pinned libraries and existing stage contracts; see the report and its assigned route.

items.name: Progression bound for the Kraus mu factors
items.statement: Under H, both mu(M_a) and mu(lcm(M_a,4)) are <=2^8*log(k)*exp(1.000081*k).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.1, p. 365 (Tenenbaum Theorem 9 and following remark)
items.note: Application adapter using the generic Euler-product bound in item 151 and the first Frey level bound. Keep this in the progression roadmap so the analytic supplier does not depend back on the Frey application.

items.name: Schoenfeld explicit Chebyshev bound
items.statement: For x>0, theta(x)=sum_{p prime,p<=x}log p < 1.000081*x.
items.locator: Equation (10), p. 362; Schoenfeld 1976, concluding note p. 360
items.note: The paper's p.160 reference is inconsistent with the cited article's pagination. Do not confuse Mathlib's weaker theta<=log(4)*x with this constant.

items.name: Projective point count and integer Frobenius trace
items.statement: For a Weierstrass model W over finite F_q, pointCount counts affine equation solutions plus the point at infinity; a_q=q+1-pointCount. On an elliptic model this is q+1 minus the cardinality of its point group.
items.note: Pinned PointCount.lean read, including the singular-model counting convention.

items.name: Hasse bound
items.statement: For an elliptic curve over F_q, a_q^2<=4*q, equivalently |a_q|<=2*sqrt(q).
items.note: Audit says point count exists but unconditional Hasse does not at these pins; determinant hypotheses in a partial endgame are not discharged.

items.name: Supersingularity criterion at a prime at least five
items.statement: For E/F_p, p>=5 prime, geometric supersingularity is equivalent to a_p(E)=0. Over F_(p^r) the criterion is p|a_(p^r), not generally equality to zero.
items.note: Source-specific statement audited against the pinned libraries and existing stage contracts; see the report and its assigned route.

items.name: Trace zero for the j=1728 reduction
items.statement: If p=3 modulo 4 is prime and u is nonzero in F_p, the curve y^2=x(x-u)(x+u) has a_p=0.
items.note: Direct pairing x with -x in its quadratic-character point count proves it; no CM distribution theorem or GRH is needed.

items.name: Von Mangoldt weight
items.statement: Lambda(m)=log p if m=p^r for a prime p and r>=1, and 0 otherwise (including m=0,1).
items.note: Definitions/statements in VonMangoldt.lean read at the pin.

items.name: Dirichlet conductor, primitivity and quadratic values
items.statement: A Dirichlet character at positive modulus N is zero on nonunits. Its conductor is the least divisor through which it factors; primitive means conductor=N; quadratic means its values lie in {0,1,-1}. The principal character has conductor 1 even when represented at larger modulus.
items.note: Exact definitions in DirichletCharacter/Basic.lean and MulChar/Basic.lean read. Principal characters represented at q_i in Theorem 6 must be called characters of modulus q_i, not conductor q_i.

items.name: Primitive character of a rational squareclass
items.statement: For u in Q^*, choose its signed squarefree integer representative d and fundamental discriminant D=d if d=1 mod 4, otherwise D=4d. The Kronecker character chi_D is primitive of conductor |D|, agrees with (u/p) at odd primes outside the support of u, and has squarefree odd conductor and 2-part at most 8. The class of 1 gives conductor 1.
items.note: Existing Legendre/small-modulus characters, Int.IsFundamentalDiscr and Tau Ceti prime-discriminant characters are ingredients, not this full classification/primitive-conductor bridge.

items.name: Quadratic-twist trace comparison
items.statement: For odd p and E/F_p with a nonzero twist parameter D, a_p(E^D)=(D/p)*a_p(E); in particular twisting preserves trace zero.
items.note: Reviewer correction: RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0, which the accepted restructure RS-30 made part of "Elliptic curves, Part II", plans "for a quadratic character construct the existing quadratic twist and prove every local Euler-factor comparison, including bad primes"; at a good odd prime that comparison is a_p(E^D) = (D/p)·a_p(E). Tau Ceti has the ingredients (quadraticTwistPointEquiv_map_eq_quadraticCharacter_smul_map, ncard_setOf_map_frobeniusAlgHom_eq_self) but no trace identity.

items.name: Chebyshev sums used by the argument
items.statement: psi(X)=sum_{1<=m<=X}Lambda(m), theta(X)=sum_{p<=X}log p; theta(X;a,h) restricts the latter prime sum to p=a modulo h, with gcd(a,h)=1.
items.note: Ordinary psi/theta are library (item 138); the AP wrapper and exact finite-interval conventions are the additional application definition.

items.name: Case-I and Case-II partition of Legendre parameters
items.statement: Let S_sq=-Q^2 union 2*Q^2. Case I consists of triples whose associated full-two-torsion curve has some Legendre parameter outside S_sq; Case II consists of those whose six parameters all lie in S_sq. These partition A.
items.note: Source-specific statement audited against the pinned libraries and existing stage contracts; see the report and its assigned route.

items.name: Case-II positive parameter normalization
items.statement: In Case II one can choose a parameter lambda and positive rationals t,v with lambda=2*t^2, 1-lambda=2*v^2, hence 2*t^2+2*v^2=1.
items.note: Source-specific statement audited against the pinned libraries and existing stage contracts; see the report and its assigned route.

items.name: Order-four witness in the quadratic twist
items.statement: Over F_p with p=5 mod 8, suppose t,v are nonzero and 2*t^2+2*v^2=1; put lambda=2*t^2 and choose i with i^2=-1. On F'_lambda:y^2=x(x-2)(x-2lambda), the point P=(4*i*t*v+2lambda,8*i*t*v*(t+i*v)) satisfies 2P=(2lambda,0), hence has order 4, and its third descent coordinate is the squareclass of 4*i*t*v.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 6.6, p.371; corrected order-four witness
items.note: Corrected coordinates, not a literal transcription: the printed second coordinate fails at p=5,t=v=2,i=3, where x=4,y=4 gives y^2=1 but x(x-2)(x-2lambda)=4. The replacement follows from halving (2lambda,0) using square roots 2t and 2iv, and is tested by exact finite-field membership/doubling. See report D15.

items.name: Mod-eight prime mass
items.statement: With epsilon=0.002811, for a=3 or 5 and k>=2*10^10, theta(k;a,8)-theta(k/2;a,8)>=(1-3*epsilon)*k/8.
items.note: Source at endpoints x>=10^10; both classes are needed. This is quantitative and not supplied by Dirichlet's infinitude theorem.

items.name: Prime powers do not erase the character-sum margin
items.statement: For k>=2*10^10, the prime-power mass psi(k)-theta(k)-psi(k/2)+theta(k/2) is smaller than (((1-3*0.002811)/8)-0.1239)*k. Thus an absolute prime-weighted sum >=(1-3*epsilon)k/8 implies an absolute Lambda-weighted sum >0.1239*k.
items.locator: §6 end of Case I, pp. 369–370; Schoenfeld Theorem 6*, (5.3*)–(5.4*)
items.note: Alternative verified proof from 65: psi(k)-theta(k)<=1.000081*(sqrt(k)+(log(k)/log(2))*k^(1/3)). Dividing by k gives a decreasing function for k>=2*10^10; at this threshold it is <0.000012<0.000045875, the available margin. Dropping the nonnegative lower-end prime-power mass preserves the bound. This repair does not require Schoenfeld's sharper Theorem 6*. Reviewer: a proof needing neither item 65 nor Schoenfeld is available from pinned Mathlib: Chebyshev.psi_sub_theta_le_psi_add_psi_add_psi (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Chebyshev.lean:584, psi-theta <= psi(x^(1/2))+psi(x^(1/3))+psi(x^(1/5))), Chebyshev.psi_le (line 444, psi x <= log 4*x+2*sqrt(x)*log x) and Chebyshev.theta_le_psi (line 404) give a prime-power mass below 1.05e-5*k at k=2e10, under the 4.5875e-5*k margin, with the ratio decreasing in k. The item stays missing: the numerical inequality itself is not a declaration.

items.name: Four-character projection in Case I
items.statement: Assume Hplus and choose lambda outside S_sq. In fact lambda lies in none of ±Q^2,±2Q^2. Let mu_1,...,mu_4 correspond to lambda,-lambda,2lambda,-2lambda. On odd primes away from support, mu1-mu2-mu3+mu4 equals 4*(lambda/p) for p=3 mod 8 and 0 otherwise. Hence one of these four primitive characters has the required absolute prime-sum lower bound and nontrivial odd conductor.
items.note: The signed linear combination yields a lower bound for at least one absolute sum, not necessarily a positive sum for a prescribed character.

items.name: Quartic descent input
items.statement: If T,V,U are positive coprime integers and T^4+V^4=2*U^2, then T=V=U=1.
items.note: The classical descent is an explicit prerequisite proof task. Do not confuse it with Fermat's equation x^4+y^4=z^4 or cite that weaker theorem.

items.name: Lemos rational-isogeny uniformity
items.statement: If E/Q has End_(Qbar)(E)=Z and admits a nontrivial cyclic Q-isogeny, then rho(E,ell) is surjective onto GL_2(F_ell) for every prime ell>37.
items.locator: §6 final paragraph, p. 373; Lemos Theorem 1.1, arXiv v2 p. 2
items.note: Original theorem and assumptions inspected. This is a proved restricted uniformity result; no general Serre uniformity conjecture is used.

items.name: Integrality of a CM j-invariant
items.statement: The j-invariant of an elliptic curve with geometric complex multiplication is an algebraic integer. In particular, for a CM elliptic curve over Q it is an integer.
items.note: CM.3 explicitly proves integrality of singular moduli; its reviewed audit reports this absent at the pin. The residual-image consequence is split into item 148.

items.name: CM exclusion for the progression Frey curve
items.statement: Under H, E_a is not CM: j(E_a)=2^8*(a_a^2-b_a*c_a)^3/(a_a*b_a*c_a)^2. Integral j and pairwise coprimality force all three a_a,b_a,c_a to be signed powers of 2, and a+b+c=0 forces two equal. The alternatives imply d|3 or d=0, contrary to Lemma 4.1/nontriviality.
items.note: The rational j formula agrees with Delta=16(abc)^2; this is another regression check on correction D1.

items.name: Case-II conductor support and exclusion
items.statement: Under Hplus and item 76, choose one primitive character in the squareclasses omega*t*v, omega in {±1,±2}, by projection to primes 5 mod 8 and item 35. Its odd conductor divides M_a. If that odd conductor were 1, then t*v is a square or twice a square; the parity of 2*T^2+2*V^2=U^2 rules out the latter, item 81 gives lambda=1/2, and items 82–84 and 148 contradict the residual comparison.
items.note: The choice also obeys the same absolute-sum margin as Case I. This is the local proof of the simultaneous package, not a different unrelated family.

items.name: Largest prime divisor and odd part
items.statement: For N>1 let P(N) be the largest prime divisor of N, and let N^odd=N/2^v_2(N) be the odd part of N.
items.note: Reviewer correction (REV-PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20): the definitional clause is in pinned Mathlib. P(N) is Nat.maxPrimeFac (Mathlib/Data/Nat/MaxPrimeFac.lean:39), with Nat.isGreatest_maxPrimeFac (1<n → IsGreatest {p | p.Prime ∧ p ∣ n} (maxPrimeFac n), line 66); N^odd is the notation ordCompl[2] N = N / 2^(N.factorization 2) (Mathlib/Data/Nat/Factorization/Defs.lean:331, documented as the odd part). The junk value maxPrimeFac 1 = 1 is never used, since P is applied only to N>1. The conductor bound formerly in this item is item 152.

items.name: Two-real-zero inequality
items.statement: There is an effective absolute c_star>0 such that if distinct real primitive quadratic characters of conductors N1,N2>1 have real zeros beta1,beta2, then min(beta1,beta2)<1-3*c_star/log(N1*N2).
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Uniqueness and simplicity of an exceptional zero
items.statement: For that same c_star, a primitive nonprincipal quadratic character of conductor N has at most one real zero in (1-c_star/log N,1), and any such zero is simple.
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Effective character prime-number estimate
items.statement: For a primitive nonprincipal character chi of conductor N>1 and X sufficiently large, sum_{m<=X}chi(m)*Lambda(m)=-X^beta/beta+O(X*exp(-c*log X/(sqrt(log X)+log N))*(log N)^4), with the beta term only when an exceptional zero exists; c>0 and the implied constant are absolute and effective.
items.note: Used nonprincipal specialization only. The printed principal N=1 case needs a log(2N)-type convention to avoid a zero error factor; no false exact psi(X)=X assertion is exported.

items.name: Small-conductor exclusion of real zeros
items.statement: For every primitive Dirichlet character of conductor q<=400000 there are no real zeros of L(s,chi) with 0<s<1. In particular there are no exceptional conductors in this range.
items.locator: §7 proof of Proposition 7.2, p. 376; Platt Theorems 7.1–7.2
items.note: Original computational result inspected: bounded-height GRH plus separately certified nonvanishing at 1/2 (up to 2000000). Height zero is included. A future formal proof must check interval-arithmetic/Turing certificates; empirical floating-point output is not a library theorem.

items.name: Many small smooth characters force a bound on k
items.statement: Under Hplus, for every c2>10, if B subset A has |B|>17*log k, its chosen characters are pairwise distinct, P(N_a)<=k^(7/16), and N_a<k^c2, then k<=k2(c2) effectively.
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Smooth-modulus short-character estimate
items.statement: Let r>=1, let pi_i be Dirichlet characters represented at positive moduli q_i, and write q=q_1>1. Suppose q is squarefree, gcd(q,q_2...q_r)=1, and pi_1 is primitive. For R>=max(q_2,...,q_r,q^(1/4))*q^(5/4), any interval (M,M+R] satisfies |sum_m product_i pi_i(m)|<=4*R*(tau(q)^(r^2)/q)^(2^(-r)); for r=1 the maximum is q^(1/4).
items.note: Modulus replaces printed 'conductor' for the possibly principal later factors, as the actual application requires. Absolute bars and exponent 2^(-r) checked in page image. Original book proof/source-edition comparison remains a design preparation task.

items.name: Primitive reduction of a Dirichlet character
items.statement: For a character chi at positive modulus M there is a primitive character at conductor(chi), and changing its level back to M recovers chi.
items.note: Actual statements read; they retain nonunit zero-extension.

items.name: Product character with its exclusion modulus
items.statement: For distinct primitive quadratic chi1,chi2 at N1,N2, put M=lcm(N1,N2), eta the primitive character inducing their product, M1=cond(eta), and M2=product of primes p|M with p not dividing M1. Then eta is nonprincipal, gcd(M1,M2)=1, M1*M2 divides M, M2 divides gcd(N1,N2), and chi1(m)*chi2(m)=eta(m)*1_{gcd(m,M2)=1} for every integer m.
items.locator: Corrected conductor decomposition for Proposition 8.2, p. 377
items.note: M is an ambient modulus, not necessarily the product character's conductor. In particular conductors 8 and 8 can multiply to conductor 4; their product does not require the false equality M=M1*M2.

items.name: Bounded CRT factor blocks
items.statement: Fix c2>0. If N_i<=k^c2 and P(N_i)<=k^(7/16), and the M1 of item 94 is >=8*k^(7/32), then for sufficiently large k the product character has a CRT factorization with one primitive odd squarefree factor q in [k^(7/32),k^(7/16)], all other moduli <=k^(7/16), and at most ceil(10*c2)+4 factors. Consequently the R0 of item 92 is <=k^(63/64)<k/2.
items.note: Greedily group odd primes, leaving residual blocks and the bounded 2-part explicit; remove modulus-one factors. This weakened finite bound suffices for the existential c3 and avoids requiring the printed nonempty last principal block when M2=1.

items.name: Effective divisor subpower bound
items.statement: For every epsilon>0 there is an effectively computable C_epsilon such that tau(n)<=C_epsilon*n^epsilon for all positive integers n; equivalently tau(n)<=n^(2epsilon) for all sufficiently large n.
items.note: Do not export the printed universal tau(q)<=q^(1/log log(3q)); e.g. q=120 contradicts it. Eventual subpower bounds suffice in both applications.

items.name: Small primitive-conductor cancellation with exclusions
items.statement: For nonprincipal primitive eta of conductor M1 and squarefree M2 coprime to M1, |sum_{k/2<m<=k}eta(m)*1_{gcd(m,M2)=1}|<=tau(M2)*M1, by Möbius inversion and complete-period cancellation. Also the direct period bound is <=M1*M2. Apply with M1<8*k^(7/32), separating M2<=k^(3/4) from larger M2.
items.note: All moduli and conductor bounds are retained; the source-specific exponent gap is not the general orthogonality identity alone.

items.name: Prime-number asymptotic used by the Gram bound
items.statement: psi(x)=x+o(x), and the quantitative PNT error can be chosen so that psi(k)-psi(k/2)=k/2+O(k/log k). Thus sum_{k/2<m<=k}Lambda(m)^2 <= (k log k)/2+O(k).
items.note: Unconditional classical PNT is planned, not available at the pins. Tau Ceti's conditional PNT transfer is not the analytic hypothesis itself.

items.name: Gram-matrix bound for the chosen characters
items.statement: Under Proposition 8.1 and pairwise cancellation 44, (1/|B|)*sum_{a in B}|sum_{k/2<m<=k}chi_a(m)*Lambda(m)|^2 <= (k log k/2+O(k))*((k+1)/(34 log k)+k^(1-c3)) = (1/68+o(1))*k^2.
items.note: The diagonal and off-diagonal bounds are separate, and 1/68<0.1239^2 is the correct comparison. The printed final comparison with the square of an already squared constant is false.

items.name: Divisibility index sets
items.statement: For I={0,...,k-1} and each prime p put I_p={i in I:p divides n+i*d}. If gcd(n,d)=1 then I_p is empty when p|d; otherwise it is one residue class modulo p and ||I_p|-k/p|<1.
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Rahman quantitative Roth threshold
items.statement: For 0<delta<1, the conclusion of item 46 holds whenever k>=exp(exp(132*log(2)/delta)).
items.note: This numerical choice is quoted explicitly in the fully read main source. Rahman's original linked PDF currently returned empty content and the former MIT URL returned 404; mark source preparation required, not independently proof-verified. Mathlib's tower bound does not certify this formula.

items.name: Rosser–Schoenfeld explicit prime-count bounds
items.statement: For x>=59, (x/log x)*(1+1/(2 log x))<pi(x)<(x/log x)*(1+3/(2 log x)).
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Explicit reciprocal-prime estimate
items.statement: There is the prime Mertens constant B=0.26149... such that for x>=286, |sum_{p<=x}1/p-log log x-B|<1/(2*(log x)^2).
items.note: Absolute value is part of the input; both endpoints are needed in the interval estimate.

items.name: Thin-prime sieve survivors
items.statement: Under Proposition 9.1 define T_pr={p prime:k^(7/16)<p<=k}, U_pr={p prime:(log k)^(1-10^(-4))<p<=10^4 log k}, and J=I minus the union of I_p over S union T_pr union U_pr. Every triple from J has conductor avoiding S and U_pr and largest conductor prime <=k^(7/16).
items.note: No prime 2 lies in S (otherwise its reciprocal alone exceeds .17) or T_pr/U_pr at the working threshold, so the uncontrolled bounded 2-part does not break avoidance.

items.name: Sieve loss and positive density
items.statement: For k>=exp(exp(10^6)), the losses from T_pr, U_pr, S are respectively <=k*log(16/7), <=k*log(1/(1-10^(-4)))+5*k*log(10)/log log k+10^4 log k, and <.17*k+1.1*k/log k. Their union has size <.9968*k, hence |J|>.0032*k.
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Survivor factorial bound after valuation deletion
items.statement: For J1 obtained from J by item 48, |J1|>.00319*k and product_{i in J1}A_i divides (k-1)!, with all its prime factors <=k^(7/16).
items.note: The text says no p>=k^(7/16), while the sieve only excludes p>k^(7/16); retain the weak endpoint, which is exactly what the subsequent product over p>k^(7/16) uses.

items.name: Smooth part of the factorial is small
items.statement: For the J1 above and k>=exp(exp(10^6)), log(product_{k^(7/16)<p<=k}p^v_p((k-1)!)) >=(9/16)*k*log k-5*k. With the explicit Stirling upper bound for (k-1)!, this gives product_{i in J1}A_i<k^(.44*k).
items.note: The weighted-prime input and Stirling remainder are separately itemized below; no unspecified asymptotic may replace the stated threshold. Reviewer: the explicit Stirling bound (item 141) is not needed here: Nat.factorial_le_pow (n! <= n^n, Mathlib/Data/Nat/Factorial/Basic.lean:183) already gives product A_i < exp((7/16)k log k + 5k) <= k^(0.44k) once log k >= 2000, which holds for k >= exp(exp(10^6)). Item 142 is still needed. Status unchanged.

items.name: Small-coefficient dense subset and selected progression
items.statement: Under Proposition 9.1's preliminary construction, set J2={i in J1:A_i<=k^139}. Then |J2|>10^(-5)*k. The quoted Roth bound has log log K0(10^(-5))=132*log(2)*10^5, which lies between 10^6 and 10^7. Thus for k>=exp(exp(10^7)), one triple in J2 has N_a<=2^8*A_i*A_j*A_h<k^418.
items.note: Corrected sufficient threshold, not the false numerical comparison printed on p.384. The Markov density bound and exponent 418 are unchanged.

items.name: Thin-prime avoidance projection
items.statement: For the single witness a constructed in item 47 (under its hypotheses), no prime in S divides N_a.
items.note: Projection of the same simultaneous existential package; not an independent choice of a.

items.name: Smooth-conductor projection
items.statement: For the single witness a constructed in item 47 (under its hypotheses), P(N_a)<=k^(7/16).
items.note: Projection of the same simultaneous existential package; not an independent choice of a.

items.name: Medium-prime gap projection
items.statement: For the single witness a constructed in item 47 (under its hypotheses), no prime p with (log k)^(1-10^(-4))<p<=10^4*log k divides N_a.
items.note: Projection of the same simultaneous existential package; not an independent choice of a.

items.name: Polynomial-conductor projection
items.statement: For the single witness a constructed in item 47 (under its hypotheses), N_a<k^418.
items.note: Projection of the same simultaneous existential package; not an independent choice of a.

items.name: Maximal family with distinct largest conductor primes
items.statement: For large k choose a nonempty inclusion-maximal B subset A whose P(N_a) are distinct, P(N_a)<=k^(7/16), N_a<k^418, and N_a avoids the open-left interval ((log k)^(1-10^(-4)),10^4 log k]. If |B|<=17 log k then sum_{a in B}1/P(N_a)>=.17; otherwise item 47 augments B.
items.note: Use the exact open-left interval supplied by Proposition 9.1; the printed switch to a closed-left interval is not justified.

items.name: Maximal-family dichotomy closes the original proof
items.statement: For B in 113, either |B|>17 log k and Proposition 8.1 bounds k, or its subfamily D with P(N_a)<=(log k)^(1-10^(-4)) has reciprocal mass >=.1683>.166, since the complementary mass is <=.0017. Apply Proposition 7.2 with c1=1/20000 to obtain the strict required smoothness and an effective bound on k.
items.locator: §10 proof of Theorem 2, p. 385; corrected endpoint dispatch
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Smooth-multiplier extension and its stated scope
items.statement: Register the extension discussed for product(n+i*d)=b*y^ell with all prime divisors of nonzero b at most tau*k for a fixed tau<1/2. The paper announces that its arguments extend in this range but supplies no separate quantified theorem or full proof; it expressly does not handle all P(b)<=k.
items.note: Design target/statement register, not a proved theorem with invented constants. b=±1 is interpreted by its empty prime support.

items.name: Bounded-height Landau–Page theorem
items.statement: There is an effective absolute c>0 such that among primitive Dirichlet characters of moduli q<=T, T>=2, there is at most one zero rho=beta+i*t with |t|<=T and beta>1-c/log T. Any exception is a simple real zero of a real character.
items.locator: §12 opening, p. 386; Bombieri §5 p.39; Iwaniec–Kowalski Theorem 5.26
items.note: The height restriction omitted in the opening prose must be restored. It is explicitly present in Bombieri's primary statement inspected here.

items.name: Selberg zero-density input
items.statement: For epsilon>0, Q>=2, T>=2, and 1/2<=sigma<=1, sum_{q<=Q} sum_{chi primitive mod q} N(sigma,T,chi) <<_epsilon (Q^(5+epsilon)*T^(3+epsilon))^(1-sigma), with effective constants; if the source count omits the possible exceptional zero, add 1 to the right-hand side.
items.locator: §12 proof of Proposition 12.1, p. 386; Bombieri §5 remark after Theorem 14, p.40
items.note: N counts zeros with multiplicity, beta>=sigma and |Im rho|<=T. The +1 allowance preserves the application and respects Bombieri's exceptional-zero convention.

items.name: Quadratic real-zero separation from one
items.statement: For q>=3 and a quadratic Dirichlet character modulo q, a real zero beta>0 satisfies beta<=1-40/(sqrt(q)*(log q)^2).
items.note: Original statement and its §6.1 proof inspected. Small q uses certified zero computations; larger q uses L(1,chi) and derivative bounds. No ineffective Siegel constant is substituted.

items.name: Polylogarithmic number of exceptional moduli
items.statement: For Q(k) in 49 and sufficiently large k, |Q(k)| << (log k)^61, with effective implied constant.
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Minimum exceptional modulus
items.statement: For sufficiently large k, every q in Q(k) satisfies q>=log k.
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Only one small exceptional modulus
items.statement: For Q(k) there is at most one element below T=k^(delta/log log k), where delta=c/3>0; all other elements are at least T.
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Nonexceptional primitive character has a small weighted half-interval sum
items.statement: For sufficiently large k, primitive nonprincipal chi of conductor q<=k^4 with q not in Q(k) satisfies |sum_{k/2<m<=k}chi(m)*Lambda(m)| << k/log k, effectively and uniformly.
items.locator: Proposition 12.2, p.387; repaired hypothesis and zero-sum estimate
items.note: Keep the truncation height T throughout, not the printed switch to Q. Subtract the two explicit formulas before bounding to control zeros near 0; item 139 and report D10.

items.name: Exceptional divisibility indices
items.statement: For coprime nonzero integers a,d, let N_bad(a,d)={n in {0,...,k-1}: some q in Q(k) has a divisor r>=q^(1/3)/2 with r dividing a+n*d}.
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Exceptional index set is sparse
items.statement: For the set of 123, |N_bad(a,d)| << k/(log k)^(1/4), with an effective bound uniform in coprime nonzero a,d.
items.note: Corrected proof retains k/r+1: the +1 contributions are bounded by k^(1/3)*(log k)^61 using tau(q)<<q^(1/12) and q<=k^4, and are negligible at this scale.

items.name: One addendum triple with both conductor size and avoidance
items.statement: Under Hplus and for sufficiently large k, there is one a=(i,j,h) in A whose three indices avoid N_bad(n,d) and for which N_a<=8*A_i*A_j*A_h<=k^4.
items.locator: §12 final paragraph, p.388; explicit simultaneous-witness repair
items.note: Proof supplied in report using maximal-valuation deletion, disjoint consecutive triples, and their average logarithmic product. Do not combine two independent existence assertions.

items.name: Odd-conductor divisibility detects an exceptional index
items.statement: For the triple of 125, N_a^odd divides A_i*A_j*A_h and N_a<=8*N_a^odd. Therefore product_{r in {i,j,h}}gcd(N_a,A_r)>=N_a/8, so one gcd is at least N_a^(1/3)/2. If N_a were in Q(k), that index would belong to N_bad(n,d), a contradiction.
items.note: No equality with the largest odd squarefree divisor is needed or generally justified.

items.name: Granville addendum contradiction
items.statement: For sufficiently large k, choose the same triple from 125. Item 126 gives N_a not in Q(k), while N_a<=k^4 and N_a^odd!=1. Then 122 contradicts the lower bound >.1239*k in 37. This gives an alternative effective k0 for Theorem 2, without Roth or smooth-modulus short-sum estimates.
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Composite-exponent reduction
items.statement: If ell>=2 is an integer and p is a prime divisor of ell, a primitive progression solution with right side y^ell gives one of prime exponent p and new power variable y^(ell/p). Once y is restricted to finitely many integers with |y|>1, it has only finitely many representations as a nontrivial perfect power.
items.note: Treat y=±1 and zero separately. This is not a bound on composite ell from a bound on only its largest prime divisor.

items.name: Fixed-exponent progression finiteness input
items.statement: For each fixed k>=5 and integer ell>=2, the integer solutions of product_{i<k}(n+i*d)=y^ell with gcd(n,d)=1 and yd!=0 form a finite set. This suffices for item 50 when k0 is increased to at least 5.
items.note: Original Darmon–Granville Corollary 2.1 and its complete §2.1 proof, pp.520–521, read: the theorem has m>=2,k>=3,m+k>=6; the strict genus argument applies to m+k>=7, hence our k>=5. The finite coefficient systems and projective scaling/primitive normalization bridge must be retained, including signs.

items.name: Elliptic residual Galois representation
items.statement: For E/Q and prime ell, the G_Q action on geometric ell-torsion gives a continuous two-dimensional F_ell representation (up to basis); its determinant is the mod-ell cyclotomic character, and for odd ell it is odd.
items.note: Two-dimensionality and determinant require the torsion/Weil-pairing theorems; a generic group action does not supply them.

items.name: Unconditional elliptic modularity supplier
items.statement: Every elliptic curve E/Q has a normalized weight-two newform with rational coefficients, trivial nebentypus and exact level N_E, with matching local factors and Tate-module realizations.
items.note: Already owned; never re-prove the Wiles/BCDT or Serre theorem inside the progression roadmap.

items.name: First Frey large-prime discriminant divisibility
items.statement: Under 14, for every prime p>=k, ell divides v_p(Delta(E_a)).
items.note: A nonempty A implies k>=3, so such p is odd; g is a p-unit and correction D1 does not change the valuation.

items.name: First Frey odd level is squarefree
items.statement: Under 18, M_a^odd is squarefree.
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: First Frey primorial divisibility
items.statement: Under 18, M_a divides 2^7*product_{q prime,q<=k}q.
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Second Frey large-prime discriminant divisibility
items.statement: Under 20, if p>=k is prime with p not dividing kappa, then ell divides v_p(Delta(E_i)).
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Second Frey local test actually used in the two-term case
items.statement: For the quadruple (i,i+1,i+p-1,i+p) in Lemma 4.1, with p in (k/2,k], p not dividing d and p dividing both endpoint terms, p|A, p does not divide B*kappa*d, and ell|v_p(A). Hence v_p(c4(E_i))=0 and v_p(Delta(E_i))>0 is divisible by ell; E_i is minimal with multiplicative reduction at p.
items.note: p>=k is not needed here: c4=16*kappa*(4*kappa*d^2-3*A) is nonzero modulo this odd p. This repairs the apparent range gap with Lemma 3.4.

items.name: Second Frey reduced-level divisibility
items.statement: Under 23, M_i divides 2^7*3^5*kappa^2*product_{q prime,q<=k}q^2.
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Ordinary Chebyshev carriers
items.statement: For real X, psi(X)=sum_{1<=n<=floor(X)}Lambda(n) and theta(X)=sum_{p prime,p<=floor(X)}log p.
items.note: Actual pinned Chebyshev.lean definitions read; no asymptotic or numerical prime theorem follows from these definitions.

items.name: Half-interval explicit formula and low-zero-safe bound
items.statement: For primitive nonprincipal chi of conductor q, sufficiently large integer k and 2<=T<=k, a truncated explicit formula on (k/2,k] has zero contributions -(k^rho-(k/2)^rho)/rho for nontrivial zeros |Im rho|<=T, with error O(k*log^2(qk)/T+log^2(qk)). Moreover |(k^rho-(k/2)^rho)/rho|<=C*k^Re(rho)*min(1,1/|rho|) for 0<Re(rho)<1. The local zero-count bound gives sum_{|Im rho|<=T}min(1,1/|rho|)<<log^2(q(T+2)).
items.locator: §12 proof of Proposition 12.2, p.387; explicit repaired interface
items.note: Subtract at the same height before absolute values, absorbing endpoint weights in the error. This avoids a false uniform bound on sum 1/|rho| near rho=0. Original Iwaniec–Kowalski Prop.5.25 edition and exceptional/constant terms must be checked before blueprint proof leaves are executable.

items.name: One residue-class count including its boundary
items.statement: For gcd(a,d)=1 and positive r, the number of 0<=n<k with r|(a+n*d) is 0 if gcd(r,d)>1, otherwise at most k/r+1.
items.note: For r>k, k/r cannot replace k/r+1 by a uniform constant multiple: a single multiple may remain.

items.name: Explicit Stirling upper bound
items.statement: For integer m>=1, m!<=sqrt(2*pi*m)*(m/e)^m*exp(1/(12*m)).
items.note: Pinned Mathlib Stirling.log_stirlingSeq_sdiff_le and tendsto_stirlingSeq_sqrt_pi were read: they supply the successive-difference estimate and limit, not this packaged global upper bound. Telescope from m to M, bound the tail by 1/(12m), pass to the limit, then exponentiate. This is a short adapter, not a second Stirling asymptotic proof.

items.name: Weighted-prime sum input to the factorial estimate
items.statement: For x>=319, with the same absolute constant E at both endpoints, log x+E-1/(2 log x)<sum_{p<=x}(log p)/p<log x+E+1/(2 log x). Therefore for x>=y>=319 the prime sum over y<p<=x is greater than log(x/y)-1/(2 log x)-1/(2 log y).
items.note: Rosser–Schoenfeld (1962), Theorem 6, p.70, equations (3.21)–(3.22), inspected as a page image. The common constant cancels; the report derives the 5k error without assuming an unspecified O(1).

items.name: Case-I lower prime sum before prime powers
items.statement: Under Hplus and Case I, one of the four characters in 80 obeys |sum_{k/2<p<=k}chi(p)*log p| >=(1-3*.002811)*k/8.
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Case-II lower prime sum before prime powers
items.statement: Under Hplus and Case II, applying the mod-8 projection to omega*t*v and the sign condition of Lemma 6.6 produces one character with |sum_{k/2<p<=k}chi(p)*log p| >=(1-3*.002811)*k/8.
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Nonexceptional smooth conductor gives an effective small sum
items.statement: Under Proposition 7.2 and for a nonexceptional chi_a, log N_a<1.07*(log k)^(1-c1), and its half-interval Lambda sum is O(k*exp(-c'*(log k)^min(c1,1/2))*(log k)^4), hence o(k) effectively.
items.locator: §7 proof, p.375; corrected exponent for general c1
items.note: The source writes exponent c1 for every 0<c1<1; the denominator sqrt(log k)+log N only proves min(c1,1/2). Its used c1 near 10^(-4) is unchanged.

items.name: Exceptional conductor chain violates the computed range
items.statement: For the D of 42, if all chosen characters are exceptional, order conductors N1<...<Ns. Then Nj>N1^(2^(j-1)) and sum 1/P(Nj)<(2/.94)/log N1<2.13/log N1. The .166 lower bound forces N1<=373743<400000, contradicting 90.
items.note: Compared with pinned declarations and existing stage scope; see the report for the evidence and route.

items.name: Character product conductor divisibility
items.statement: For characters chi,psi at one positive modulus, conductor(chi*psi) divides lcm(conductor(chi),conductor(psi)); equality is not asserted.
items.note: Actual pinned statement read; this supports but does not by itself prove the coprime exclusion factorization in 94.

items.name: CM residual image in a Cartan normalizer
items.statement: If E/Q has geometric CM by an imaginary quadratic order O and ell is prime not dividing discr(O), its image on E[ell] is contained in the normalizer of a Cartan subgroup of GL_2(F_ell). For j=1728 this applies at every odd ell. At ell>37 this is a proper subgroup and is incompatible with surjectivity.
items.locator: §6 pp.372–373; CM action and Galois-conjugation input
items.note: Use CM.4 for the actual order action and Tate-module components; the finite residual centralizer/normalizer adapter and discriminant hypothesis are additional explicit source material.

items.name: Certified-threshold version of the simultaneous conductor witness
items.statement: Assume Hplus and k>=exp(exp(10^7)). For every set S of primes <=k with sum_{p in S}1/p<.17, there is one a in A satisfying all four conclusions of item 47: avoidance of S, P(N_a)<=k^(7/16), avoidance of ((log k)^(1-10^(-4)),10^4 log k], and N_a<k^418.
items.note: All earlier estimates hold at the increased threshold; item 108 now legitimately applies the quoted Roth bound. Theorem 2 asks only for an effective unspecified k0, so this correction preserves the main target. Independent review must distinguish this repair from the literal sharper source claim in 47.

items.name: Coefficient-prime bridge for the progression Kraus application
items.statement: Under H, for every first-family Frey curve E_a and residual prime ell, the irreducible residual representation has Serre weight 2 and prime-to-ell Artin conductor equal to the reduced level M_a of item 18. In particular ell does not divide M_a.
items.note: Because ell>k, the first model is semistable at ell; if multiplicative, ell divides its minimal discriminant valuation. Apply the precise finite-flat/weight-two and local conductor criteria of R20.3–R20.4. This comparison is not licensed merely by the quotient formula in 04.

items.name: Explicit prime Euler-product bound
items.statement: For real x>=10^8, product_{p prime,p<=x}(1+1/p)<=2*log x.
items.locator: §5 proof of Lemma 5.1, p.365; alternate direct input from Rosser–Schoenfeld Theorem 8 (3.29), p.70
items.note: Bound this product by product(1-1/p)^(-1)<exp(gamma)*log x*(1+1/(2 log^2 x)); the latter is <2 log x at x>=10^8. This avoids requiring an uninspected Tenenbaum constant and does not duplicate the progression-specific mu specialization.

items.name: Quadratic primitive conductors are at most eight times their odd part
items.statement: If N is the conductor of a primitive quadratic Dirichlet character, then N<=8*N^odd, i.e. v_2(N)<=3.
items.locator: §§6–8, pp. 366, 375 (used with N=2^kappa*N_1, kappa in {0,1,2} as printed in the proof of Lemma 7.3; split from item 86 by the reviewer)
items.note: Split from item 86 by the reviewer. Neither pinned tree states the 2-adic exponent bound for primitive quadratic conductors; Mathlib has DirichletCharacter.conductor and MulChar.IsQuadratic but no classification of primitive quadratic characters by fundamental discriminants. Routed with item 72 (primitive character of a rational squareclass) to AnalyticNumberTheory, route 2.
